title: Social-Credit + : AI Driven Social Media Credit Scoring Platform

bias_targets.methodology: The paper addresses the systemic exclusion of "unbanked" or "thin-file" borrowers in traditional credit scoring by conceptually evaluating a system (Social-Credit+) that uses multimodal alternative data (social media text, images, and network graphs) to provide financial inclusion for lower-income or emerging market populations.

The authors propose incorporating fairness constraints during model training to ensure content flagging (e.g., detecting alcohol or gambling) is applied uniformly across users without exploiting religion as a protected attribute, though empirical measurement is deferred to future audits.

The system design includes proposed bias mitigation techniques (fairness constraints) to prevent the AI from using social data to discriminate based on user ethnicity, ensuring uniform application of credit rules regardless of ethnic background.
